why: OUR LANGUAGES DISAGREE: `read_string` means opposite things in C and Rust. `rclc_cdr_read_string(ptr, end, origin, value, max_len)` COPIES into a caller-sized `char[max_len]` and NUL-terminates; Rust's `CdrReader::read_string` returns `&'a str` borrowed out of the receive buffer, zero-copy. C's borrowing equivalent exists under a different verb entirely -- `rclc_cdr_borrow_string` in `rclc/detail/view.h` -- so the same two operations are spelled (read=copy, borrow=view) in C and (read=view, deserialize=copy) in Rust. Both behaviours are needed (the copy is what an `inline`-mode field wants, the view is RFC-0033 `view` mode); one word should not name both. Phase 379 W5. The extension verdict itself is `c:cdr_read_*`.
